name: Foreground service types (Android 14)
plain: Every foreground service must declare a purpose and hold the matching permission.
meaning: Forces apps to state why they keep running (location, camera, media, phone call). The type decides which hardware and permissions the service can use, so it shows purpose to reviewers.

android.prompt_ui: Notification required; microphone, camera, location need their own runtime grant while in use
android.store_policy: Play: FGS type declaration form for apps targeting 34
android.note: Types: camera, connectedDevice, dataSync, health, location, mediaPlayback, mediaProjection, microphone, phoneCall, remoteMessaging, shortService, specialUse, systemExempted; mediaProcessing added in 15

ios.persistence: Per mode; app suspended when work ends
ios.api_surface: UIBackgroundModes: audio, location, voip, bluetooth-central, bluetooth-peripheral, fetch, remote-notification, processing, external-accessory, nearby-interaction

limits.headline: Can run long Android background tasks, but only for a declared purpose with a notification
limits.user_action: You start something long, like playing music, tracking a run, or syncing a big file
can: Keep playing audio, tracking location or syncing data while the screen is off
Show you a notification that says the work is running
Use the camera, microphone or location in the background, but only after you allowed each one
cannot: Start a background service from nowhere without a notification
Use the microphone, camera or location without their own permission
Pick any purpose it likes; Android 14 makes each service declare one type and checks it
Match this on iPhone, where background modes need an Apple approved setting instead
limits.reach_label: Ongoing, but tied to a stated purpose
limits.differs: Android uses service types with a visible notification. iPhone uses background modes set up in Xcode.

story.what_it_is: Android makes every always-running app task state its purpose, like navigation or music.

marketing.name: Foreground service types
marketing.pitch: Android 14 requires apps to declare why a service keeps running, such as media playback or location.

story.for_you: You see this as a persistent notification, such as a music player or a navigation arrow. It tells you an app is allowed to keep working while you do something else.
story.for_makers: Makers must pick the right label and get the matching permission. Google and reviewers use the label to check an app is not hiding battery heavy work behind a vague reason.

use_cases.example: A navigation app keeps turn by turn guidance running with the screen off using the location type.
A streaming app keeps playing with the phone locked using the media playback type.
A driver app keeps sharing live position during a trip while you check messages in another app.
A cycling app records your route and heart rate through the whole ride using location and health types.
A calling app keeps your microphone live during a voice call after you leave the app.
A cloud gaming or remote play app keeps its stream alive while you answer a text.

risks: Apps can misuse loose labels like special use
story.android_note: Required from Android 14. Each type needs its own permission, and camera, mic and location still need your tap.
story.ios_note: iOS uses background modes in Xcode instead, which are reviewed by Apple.

abuse: Using a loose type like specialUse to stay alive

history.change: Foreground service type and matching permission mandatory
mediaProcessing type added; BOOT_COMPLETED receivers cannot start dataSync, camera, mediaPlayback, phoneCall, mediaProjection or microphone FGS
